# Rut.ts

> A modern TypeScript library for handling Chilean RUT (Rol Único Tributario) validation, formatting, cleaning, and generation with full type safety.

Rut.ts provides a comprehensive set of utilities for working with Chilean RUTs - the unique tax identification numbers used throughout Chile. The library supports validation (including strict mode for suspicious patterns), a branded `Rut` type narrowed by a type guard (`isValidRut`), a typed `InvalidRutError`, formatting (both standard and incremental for real-time input), masking for safe logging (`mask`), validity-aware comparison (`equals`), cleaning, decomposition, configurable random generation, and verifier digit calculation. It's fully typed, tree-shakeable, supports both ESM and CommonJS, and runs in Node.js (>= 20), the browser, Deno, and Bun. The RUT format follows the pattern `XX.XXX.XXX-Y` where the verifier digit is calculated using the Modulo 11 algorithm.

As of **v4.0.0** (a breaking release focused on production identity hardening), `validate()` and `isRutLike()` accept only three canonical shapes — compact (`123456785`), compact + hyphen (`12345678-5`), and canonical dotted (`12.345.678-5`), with optional surrounding whitespace. The dotted shape requires its verifier hyphen: `12.345.6785` (dots but no hyphen) is rejected, as is any non-canonical dot grouping that 3.x tolerated (`12.345678-5`, `12345.678-5`). As of **v5.0.0** — the final-shape major, after which the API contract is frozen — leading-zero padding is also rejected by the acceptance predicates `validate()`/`isValidRut()`/`isRutLike()`: a canonical RUT carries no leading zeros, so `012.345.678-5` and `0012345678` are non-canonical and return `false`. For zero-padded/dirty input use the documented two-line recipe — `const rut = clean(raw, { throwOnError: false })` then `if (rut !== null && validate(rut)) accept(rut)` — which normalizes first and then proves the Modulo 11 verifier. Also as of v5.0.0, `equals()` checks validity by default — `equals('12345678-9', '12345678-9')` is now `false` (wrong verifier: not a RUT); pass `{ requireValid: false }` for the pre-5.0.0 pure shape comparison. Validity is checked on the *normalized* value, so `equals('012345678-5', '12345678-5')` is still `true` even though `validate('012345678-5')` is `false` — an intended asymmetry. The deprecated `getInvalidRutError()` was removed (catch `InvalidRutError` / check `err.code === 'INVALID_RUT'`). Input is capped at 64 characters as a security bound (not a format rule), and errors are a generic `Invalid RUT input` so Chilean ID values are never echoed into logs or traces. `clean()` and `decompose()` remain intentionally permissive for normalization (`clean('RUT: 12.345.678-5')` → `'123456785'`; it strips every non-`[0-9kK]` character wherever it sits) and must not be treated as validation — `clean` never checks the verifier digit. Review the CHANGELOG before upgrading.

Key technical details:
- **Size**: ~3.59KB minified, ~1.62KB gzipped, as measured by [bundlejs](https://bundlejs.com/?q=rut.ts) — the same live source as the README badge (the shipped ESM dist file is slightly larger; a bundler re-minifies it away)
- **Zero dependencies**: Pure TypeScript implementation
- **Safe mode**: All throwing functions support `{ throwOnError: false }` to return `null` instead of throwing (defaults frozen until a hypothetical v6)
- **Strict validation**: `validate(rut, { strict: true })` additionally rejects repeated-digit placeholder RUTs (e.g. `11.111.111-1`)
- **Secure generation**: `generate()` uses Web Crypto (`crypto.getRandomValues`, guaranteed on Node >= 20) with unbiased rejection sampling; a `Math.random()` fallback is retained only as a safety net for exotic runtimes without Web Crypto
- **Dual package**: Native ESM with CommonJS fallback
- **Type definitions**: Full TypeScript support with exported types (including `EqualsOptions`)

## Core API Functions

- [validate()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/docs/features/validate): Validate RUT format and verifier digit with optional strict mode to detect suspicious patterns
- [format()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/docs/features/format): Format RUTs with dots and hyphens, supports incremental mode for real-time input
- [clean()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/docs/features/clean): Remove formatting, special characters, and leading zeros from RUT strings
- [decompose()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/docs/features/decompose): Split a RUT into its body (numeric part) and verifier digit components
- [calculateVerifier()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/docs/features/calculate-verifier): Calculate the correct verifier digit for a given RUT body using Modulo 11
- [generate()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/docs/features/generate): Generate valid random RUT numbers for testing and development
- [getBody()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/docs/features/get-body): Extract only the body (numeric part) from a formatted or unformatted RUT
- [getVerifier()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/docs/features/get-verifier): Extract only the verifier digit from a formatted or unformatted RUT
- [isRutLike()](https://rut.arrowsw.com/docs/features/is-rut-like): Check if a string matches RUT format without full validation
- [isValidRut()](https://github.com/arrowsw/rut.ts/blob/canary/README.md): Type guard that narrows a value to the branded `Rut` type when valid (supports strict mode)
- [mask()](https://github.com/arrowsw/rut.ts/blob/canary/README.md): Mask a RUT for safe logging/display, keeping only the leading group and verifier (`12.345.678-5` → `12.***.***-5`)
- [equals()](https://github.com/arrowsw/rut.ts/blob/canary/README.md): Answer "same RUT?" across shapes — normalizes both arguments and, by default, requires the shared value to pass Modulo 11 (`{ requireValid: false }` restores the pure shape comparison)
- [InvalidRutError](https://github.com/arrowsw/rut.ts/blob/canary/README.md): Typed error (class with `code: 'INVALID_RUT'`) thrown by the safe helpers; catch it instead of matching the message text
